label: Microsoft Outlook Calendar
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Outlook Calendar

tools.name: CancelEvent
tools.description:
Cancel a meeting you organize and email a cancellation to every invitee.

Irreversible. Invitees keep a cancelled copy. Refused when nobody else is
invited. A date already called off is reported as already cancelled, and nothing
is sent for that date. this_and_future ends the series the day before the given
date, so invitees get an updated invitation instead, with no note.

Use is_organizer, attendees, event_type and series_master_id from an earlier
read to choose this tool and scope. Only events in your own mailbox, not
shared or delegated calendars.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The meeting's event_id, exactly as an earlier read returned it.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Text included verbatim in the cancellation. Defaults to no note.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: For a repeating meeting: instance (this date), series (every date) or this_and_future (this date and later). Required when it repeats. Defaults to cancelling a meeting that does not repeat.

output.description: The meeting as read before cancelling, invitees notified, whether a note was sent, and the scope applied.

note.value: Due to a scheduling conflict, I need to cancel this meeting. Apologies for any inconvenience. We will reschedule soon.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: CreateEvent
tools.description:
Create an event in the user's default calendar, or in another calendar they can edit
when calendar_id is given.

Pass calendar_id only when the user names a calendar, never matched from the subject;
otherwise the event goes on the default calendar. With calendar_id, the result echoes it.
On a calendar someone else owns, organizer_note names that person as organizer.

Set recurrence for a repeating series: start and end are the first date's, and it
needs exactly one of recurrence.end_date, recurrence.occurrence_count or
recurrence.never_ends. When the request names no end, ask the user before creating
anything. If start_date_time is not a day the pattern produces, the series starts on the
first day it does, and first_date_note says so. Every weekday is weekly on monday to
friday. A step in working days, such as every third business day, cannot be expressed:
tell the user instead of creating a nearby pattern.

Book only at a time the user gave or picked, never one you chose. If no time was given,
propose times and let the user pick first.

body is stored as plain text unless body_format says html, in which case it is
stored as markup and rendered rather than shown literally.

Copying a description from an event that was read means passing that event's
body_html as body with body_format html. Its body field is the same description
with the markup stripped, so an agenda copied from there arrives with its links,
lists and emphasis gone.

Ignores timezone offsets provided in the start_date_time and end_date_time parameters.
Instead, uses the user's default calendar timezone to filter events.
If the user has not set a timezone for their calendar, then the timezone will be UTC.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The text of the event's subject (title) line.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The description of the event. To reuse the description of an event that was read, pass that event's body_html here and set body_format to html: its body field is the same description with every link, list and emphasis stripped out, so passing that instead silently loses the formatting. Otherwise pass the text to store, which is kept as written.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The datetime of the event's start, represented in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The datetime of the event's end, represented in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored. For a repeating series, the first date's end; the last date goes in recurrence.end_date.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: Calendar ID from a calendar listing, including a shared one you can edit. Only for a calendar the user named; never inferred from the subject. Defaults to the default calendar.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The location of the event. Defaults to no location.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: The email addresses of the attendees of the event. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com. Defaults to no attendees.

parameters.name: is_online_meeting
parameters.description: Whether Outlook should host an online meeting for this event and generate its join link. Ignored when custom_meeting_url is given. Defaults to False

parameters.name: custom_meeting_url
parameters.description: A join link to use instead of one Outlook generates. It is appended to body rather than stored as an Outlook meeting, so the created event comes back with is_online_meeting False and an empty online_meeting_join_url. The link is in the description: in body when body_format is plain_text, and in body_html when it is html. Leave unset and set is_online_meeting to True to have Outlook generate one. Defaults to no custom link.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The form the body argument is written in. Set html only when the body you are passing actually carries HTML tags, as the body_html of an event that was read does. Declaring html over plain words stores them marked as markup and they render wrong. plain_text stores the body as written, escaping anything that looks like markup. Defaults to plain_text.

parameters.name: recurrence
parameters.description: How the event repeats. Only the pattern asked for, never a close substitute. Leave out the fields a frequency does not use. Defaults to a one-off event.

output.description: The created event under event, and for a series the date it first takes place.

body.value: Please review the attached agenda before joining. We will cover budget forecasts, OKR progress, and roadmap planning for the next quarter.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: FindMeetingTimes
tools.description:
Propose times when a group could meet. Books nothing. Use it to find a time, and to set up
or schedule a meeting when no time is given: offer the slots and let the user pick one.

Returns up to max_candidates slots, best first. Each slot counts how many attendees are free
and names those whose availability is unknown, so it answers per-slot who can make it.

Times are in time_zone, the user's mailbox zone. On time_zone_source "mailbox_utc" or
"fallback", confirm the zone before stating times.

A slot can include busy or out-of-office attendees; say a time works for everyone only when
availability_count shows all free. Working elsewhere counts as free.

No suggestions is not an error; empty_reason and note explain it.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: Email addresses of the people to meet, excluding yourself. Up to 20.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start of the search window in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end of the search window in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used. The window must be less than 62 days.

parameters.name: meeting_duration_minutes
parameters.description: Length of the meeting in minutes. Defaults to 30.

parameters.name: max_candidates
parameters.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return, 1-20. Defaults to 5.

parameters.name: require_my_attendance
parameters.description: Whether you must be free for a slot to be suggested. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: working: your working hours (default Mon-Fri 8am-5pm); personal: working hours plus weekends; all_hours: any time. Defaults to working.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ForwardEvent
tools.description:
Send a meeting invitation to someone who is not invited yet; they join the attendee list and the organizer is told.

Works on a meeting you organize or one you were invited to. The attendee list can be edited
only on a meeting you organize, so for someone else's meeting this is the way to bring another
person in. Any bounce goes to the organizer. Refused for a cancelled meeting, the whole series
of a repeating meeting (forward one date by its own event_id), and an event nobody else is
invited to.

Name the meeting by event_id or by event_subject. Only events in your own mailbox, and a
subject is looked up in your default calendar only.

parameters.name: recipient_emails
parameters.description: Email addresses to send the invitation to, as plain addresses such as name@example.com. Each one not already invited joins the meeting's attendee list. At least one.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the meeting to forward, exactly as an earlier read returned it. Give this or event_subject, not both. Defaults to finding the event by event_subject.

parameters.name: event_subject
parameters.description: Text from the subject of the meeting to forward, matched case-insensitively against events in the search window. Only your default calendar is searched, so an event kept on another one is reachable by event_id but not by subject. Nothing is sent unless exactly one event matches. Give this or event_id, not both. Defaults to using event_id.

parameters.name: search_start_date_time
parameters.description: Start of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to 7 days ago.

parameters.name: search_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. The window may not exceed 90 days. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to 30 days from now.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Text included verbatim in the forwarded invitation. Defaults to no note.

output.description: The meeting as read before forwarding, who it was sent to, who was already invited, and how the meeting was found.

note.value: Hi Alice and Bob, please join us for this important budget review meeting. Looking forward to your input!

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetEvent
tools.description:
Get one event from any of the user's calendars, with the calendar it is on.

event carries the subject, full body, times, location, organizer and attendees,
plus change_key (the token identifying which version
of the event this is), event_type and series_master_id (which together say
whether this is a one-off event, one date of a recurring series, or the series
itself), and online_meeting_join_url (the link that joins the online meeting,
distinct from web_link, which opens the event in Outlook).

Both forms of the description come back: body is the plain text with markup
stripped, and body_html is the stored markup, whole, which a listing row does not
carry at all. Take body_html when the formatting, links or lists matter, and
supply it as the body of a new event with body_format set to html, or it is
stored as literal text. An event with no description still returns a non-empty
body_html, because Outlook stores an empty scaffold; body being empty is what says
there is no agenda.

Use this to read an event in full, or after a listing to see a body the
listing only summarised.

start, end, organizer and response_status always come back, with their own
fields empty when Microsoft Graph returned no underlying object. An empty
start is a value the event is missing, not an event that is missing.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the event to get

output.description: The event with its full body, and the calendar it is on.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetSchedule
tools.description:
Get free/busy and calendar items in a time window for one or more people. Use it to check
a specific time. It does not propose or rank slots across a range, nor count who is free per
slot.

Times are in time_zone, the user's mailbox zone, which may be a Windows name such as "Eastern
Standard Time". On time_zone_source "mailbox_utc" or "fallback", treat times as unconfirmed
and check the intended zone before acting.

availability_view has one digit per interval from start_date_time: 0 = free or working
elsewhere, 1 = tentative, 2 = busy, 3 = out of office. schedule_items can extend past the
window. working_hours are on each person's own clock.

visibility is "readable" (an item overlaps the window), "free_on_primary_calendar" (no events
on the primary calendar; secondary calendars are not visible, so not proof of free), "denied"
(no permission), or "error" (see the row's error). Subject, location and is_private appear
only when shared with you.

parameters.name: email_addresses
parameters.description: Email addresses whose free/busy availability to check - people, rooms, resources, or distribution lists. Up to 20 entities per call, where a distribution list counts as every one of its members, so prefer naming individuals when the membership is known. Split larger groups across multiple calls. Repeated addresses are ignored, so the result may cover fewer people than were passed.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start of the window to check, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the authenticated user's calendar timezone is used.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end of the window to check, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the authenticated user's calendar timezone is used. The window must be less than 62 days.

parameters.name: availability_view_interval
parameters.description: Duration in minutes of each slot in the availability_view string (5-1440). Defaults to 30.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListCalendars
tools.description:
List all calendars the user has access to.

Returns the user's own calendars plus any shared or delegated calendars.

Use a calendar_id from the results to target a specific calendar
in other calendar tools. To find which calendar an event is on, read the event instead.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of calendars to return. Max is 200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: The pagination token to continue a previous request. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of calendars. pagination_token is absent, not empty, when no further page exists.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListEventAttachments
tools.description:
List attachment metadata for a calendar event.

Returns metadata only (name, size, type, etc.). Attachment content is not included.
Use this tool when the user wants to know what files are attached to a calendar event
or meeting.

Works for an event on any of the user's calendars, including shared ones.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar event to list attachments for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of attachments to return. Max is 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: The pagination token to continue a previous request. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: Attachment metadata without the file bytes.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListEventInstances
tools.description:
List the dates one recurring series falls on between two times.

Dates come back earliest first, a date moved on its own at its new time. To see
everything on the calendar over a stretch of time, list the calendar for that window
instead. An event that does not repeat is refused.

Cancelled dates are left out, and a date moved outside the window is not in it, so a
missing date may be either. Read an empty list against series: the window may fall
before the series starts, after it ends, or between two dates.

A non-empty pagination_token means more dates remain in the window; pass it back to
read them.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: event_id of the series or of any one of its dates.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: Window start, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS in the mailbox's time zone; any offset is ignored, and a date alone means midnight.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: Window end, same format, at most 5 years after start_date_time. A date alone means midnight, so end at the next day's midnight to include a whole day.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Dates per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: pagination_token from an earlier call, to read that window's next page. When given, the other arguments are not used. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of the series' dates inside the window.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListEventsInTimeRange
tools.description:
List everything on the user's calendars between two times.

Use this when the request is about a stretch of the calendar -- what is on
today, this week, between two clock times -- rather than about a property of
one particular event, which a filtered search answers better.

Reads the default calendar unless calendar_scope is all (every calendar in the list,
shared ones included) or listed. The same meeting can appear once per calendar it
sits on.

A pagination_token means more of the window remains; pass it for the next page.
With none, the window was read in full on searched_calendars, and an empty list means
nothing is scheduled there, not on calendars left out: check skipped_calendars or use
calendar_scope all before saying the user is free. An empty page reached through a
token means the earlier pages held every event.

Times are read in the mailbox time zone, or UTC when none is set.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored.

parameters.name: calendar_scope
parameters.description: Calendars to read: default (the default calendar), all (every calendar in the calendar list, max 20) or listed (the ids in calendars). Defaults to default.

parameters.name: calendars
parameters.description: Calendar ids from the calendar list, max 20; only with calendar_scope listed. Defaults to no ids.

parameters.name: include_cancelled
parameters.description: Include cancelled events. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max events to return, 1-200. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: pagination_token from a previous result, for its next page; pass the same dates, calendars and include_cancelled. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of the events in the window.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: RemoveEventFromMyCalendar
tools.description:
Take an event off your calendar without emailing anyone.

For a meeting someone else organizes, or your own appointment with no
invitees. Other attendees keep their copies. An organizer in your organization
sees you declined; one outside it is not told. Refused for a meeting you
organize with invitees. Irreversible.

Use is_organizer, attendees, event_type and series_master_id from an earlier
read to choose this tool and scope. A cancelled meeting stays on your calendar
with is_cancelled true, and listings hide it unless asked. Only events in your
own mailbox, not shared or delegated calendars.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The event's event_id, exactly as an earlier read returned it.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: For a repeating event: instance (this date) or series (every date). Required when it repeats. Defaults to removing an event that does not repeat.

output.description: The event as read before removal, the caller's role, what the organizer sees, and the scope applied.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: RespondToEvent
tools.description:
Accept, decline or tentatively accept a meeting someone else invited you to, and tell the organizer.

Declining takes the meeting off your calendar unless Show declined events is turned on in
Outlook, and once it is gone it cannot be answered again from here. Refused for a meeting
you organize, a cancelled meeting, and the whole series of a repeating meeting: answer one
date by its own event_id.

Name the meeting by event_id or by event_subject. Only events in your own mailbox, and a
subject is looked up in your default calendar only.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: Your answer: accepted, declined or tentative.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the meeting to answer, exactly as an earlier read returned it. Give this or event_subject, not both. Defaults to finding the event by event_subject.

parameters.name: event_subject
parameters.description: Text from the subject of the meeting to answer, matched case-insensitively against events in the search window. Only your default calendar is searched, so an event kept on another one is reachable by event_id but not by subject. Nothing is sent unless exactly one event matches. Give this or event_id, not both. Defaults to using event_id.

parameters.name: search_start_date_time
parameters.description: Start of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to 7 days ago.

parameters.name: search_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. The window may not exceed 90 days. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to 30 days from now.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Text sent to the organizer with your reply, verbatim. Needs notify_organizer true. Defaults to no note.

parameters.name: notify_organizer
parameters.description: Whether the organizer is emailed your reply. A note or a proposed time is only delivered when this is true. Set false to record your answer on your own calendar only; the organizer's tracking then keeps showing no reply. Required when the organizer did not ask for replies. Defaults to True.

parameters.name: proposed_start_date_time
parameters.description: A different start to suggest to the organizer, as a full ISO 8601 date and time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Take the date from the meeting as read; do not assume today. Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Only with declined or tentative, only when the organizer allows new times, and only with notify_organizer true. Defaults to proposing no new time.

parameters.name: proposed_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the suggested time, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), read the same way. Needs proposed_start_date_time. Defaults to keeping the meeting's current length.

output.description: The meeting after your answer, whether the answer was confirmed, and how the meeting was found.

note.value: I may be a few minutes late, but I plan to join.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SearchEvents
tools.description:
Find calendar events by what is true about them: subject text, who attends,
who organised them, importance, or whether they are online.

Use this when the request names a property of the event, even within a single day.
For a stretch of the calendar with no such property, such as Tuesday or this week,
read the time range instead.

Searches the default calendar, 90 days either side of today unless dates are given;
calendar_scope all covers every calendar in the list, shared ones included. The same
meeting can appear once per calendar it sits on. Results are in chronological order,
each body a short summary.

A pagination_token means more of the window remains: pass it for the next page, even
after an empty page, before reporting that nothing matched. With none, searched_window
was read in full on searched_calendars, and an empty result means nothing matched
there: check skipped_calendars, widen the range or search more calendars before
reporting there is none. An empty page reached through a token means the earlier
pages held every match.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Filter events whose subject contains this text (case-insensitive). Defaults to any subject.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: Filter events that include these attendees by exact email address. Multiple emails are combined with AND (all must be attendees). Defaults to any attendees.

parameters.name: organizer_name
parameters.description: Filter events organized by another specific person by their display name. Matching is case-insensitive substring against the organizer's display name. Do not use this to filter for events organized by the current authenticated user — use organized_by_me=True instead, which does not depend on knowing your own display name. Defaults to any organizer.

parameters.name: organized_by_me
parameters.description: True for the user's own events, False for others', including the owner's on a shared calendar; prefer over organizer_name for the user's own events. Defaults to any organizer.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Filter by event importance level. Defaults to any importance.

parameters.name: is_online_meeting
parameters.description: Filter on Outlook's own online-meeting flag: True keeps events Outlook hosts a meeting for, False keeps the rest. False is not the same as in person: an event run on a link pasted into its body is flagged False. Defaults to no filter.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start of the time range, in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used. Required with calendar_scope all or listed. Defaults to 90 days before today.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end of the time range, in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used. Required with calendar_scope all or listed. Defaults to 90 days after today.

parameters.name: calendar_scope
parameters.description: Calendars to search: default (the default calendar), all (every calendar in the calendar list, max 20) or listed (the ids in calendars). Defaults to default.

parameters.name: calendars
parameters.description: Calendar ids from the calendar list, max 20; only with calendar_scope listed. Defaults to no ids.

parameters.name: include_cancelled
parameters.description: Whether to include cancelled events in the results. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max events per page, up to 200. Defaults to 25, or to the token's page size when continuing.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: pagination_token from a previous result, for its next page; pass it alone or with the same filters and calendars. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of matches, with a pagination_token while more of the window remains.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: UpdateEvent
tools.description:
Change one event in the user's calendar, in place.

Returns an UpdateEventResult: the updated event in full, plus changed and
fields_changed (what was actually written, which is nothing when the event
already said what was asked for), change_key, concurrency_checked,
applied_scope, online_meeting_preserved, attendees_not_found, and the record
of how the event was resolved.

Everyone invited is mailed an updated invitation for any change this writes,
so an edit to a meeting with guests is not a quiet one.

Every input left out leaves that part of the event alone, so this changes
only what is named and never cancels, deletes or re-creates the event.
Adding or dropping a guest is merged over the people already invited rather
than replacing them; set_attendee_emails states the whole invitation list and
replaces it.

For a repeating meeting, scope is required; series takes series_master_id. There
is no scope for this date and later. Changing a series' time, time zone, all-day
setting or how often it repeats resets every date changed on its own and brings
back its cancelled dates, so it is refused while an upcoming date is cancelled;
changing only when it ends keeps those dates. recurrence changes only the parts of
the repeat rule it names. A meeting that does not repeat takes no scope; there
recurrence makes it repeat, keeping its event_id, and needs recurrence.frequency
and an end.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the event to change, exactly as an earlier read returned it. Give this or event_subject, not both. Defaults to finding the event by event_subject.

parameters.name: event_subject
parameters.description: Text from the subject of the event to change, matched case-insensitively against events in the search window. Only your default calendar is searched, so an event kept on another one is reachable by event_id but not by subject. Use this when the event is known by what it is called rather than by an identifier. Nothing is changed unless exactly one event matches. Give this or event_id, not both. Defaults to using event_id.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Required for a repeating meeting and refused for one that does not repeat: instance changes the given date, series changes every date including past ones and takes the series' own id. Defaults to no scope, which only works for an event that does not repeat.

parameters.name: search_start_date_time
parameters.description: Start of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format. Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to 7 days ago.

parameters.name: search_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format. Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. The window may not exceed 90 days. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to 30 days from now.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: New title for the event. This is what the event is called, not what it says -- the description is body. Pass an empty string to leave the event untitled. Defaults to leaving the title unchanged.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: New description for the event, replacing the existing one rather than adding to it. To keep the formatting of a description that was read, pass that event's body_html here and set body_format to html: its body field is the same description with every link, list and emphasis stripped out, so passing that instead silently flattens it. Otherwise pass the text to store, with line breaks kept. On a meeting, the block that makes it joinable is carried over and the response says what survived, so an empty string clears the words but leaves that block rather than emptying the description. Defaults to leaving the description unchanged.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: New start for the event, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored: the wall clock given is the wall clock the event lands on, read in time_zone or the mailbox's own timezone. Naming only this keeps the existing end. When event_id is a series itself, only the clock time is used; the series keeps its own first date. Defaults to leaving the start unchanged.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: New end for the event, in ISO 8601 format. Any timezone offset is ignored. Naming only this keeps the existing start, which is how a meeting is shortened or extended. When event_id is a series itself, only the clock time is used; the series keeps its own first date. Defaults to leaving the end unchanged.

parameters.name: time_zone
parameters.description: Timezone the new start and end wall clocks should be read in, as a Windows zone name such as Eastern Standard Time or an IANA name such as America/New_York. Needs start_date_time or end_date_time beside it, since a zone on its own reaches neither end of the event; whichever of the two is left out keeps the moment it already runs at. Defaults to the mailbox's own timezone.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: New location for the event, replacing whatever is there. This is where people go, not where an online meeting lives. A room booked through Outlook cannot be written over from here -- Outlook replaces the whole place when a new one is written, which would turn the booking into plain text -- so such a change is refused. Pass an empty string to clear it. Defaults to leaving the location unchanged.

parameters.name: is_all_day
parameters.description: Whether the event should occupy whole days rather than a clock time. Changing this needs start_date_time and end_date_time given alongside it, and when true both must fall at midnight, the end being the day after the last day the event covers. Defaults to leaving the all-day setting unchanged.

parameters.name: show_as
parameters.description: How the event should show to people checking the organizer's availability. Outlook labels this Show As. Defaults to leaving Show As unchanged.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: New priority for the event. Defaults to leaving the priority unchanged.

parameters.name: reminder_minutes_before_start
parameters.description: How many minutes before the start the reminder should fire. Outlook keeps the alert and its lead time as two separate settings, so asking for a reminder here turns the alert on as well -- an event carrying this lead time with its alert off is still changed. Defaults to leaving the reminder unchanged.

parameters.name: attendee_emails_to_add
parameters.description: Email addresses to invite, added to the people already invited. Everyone else keeps their place and the reply they gave. Defaults to adding nobody.

parameters.name: attendees_to_remove
parameters.description: People to uninvite, each given as an email address or as whole words from a person's name -- a first name, a surname, or both, matched against the names the guests are listed under. Part of a word does not match, so Sam does not reach Samantha. A name matching more than one guest is refused rather than guessed, an entry matching nobody is reported back while the rest of the edit still applies, and everyone actually uninvited is named in the response. Defaults to removing nobody.

parameters.name: set_attendee_emails
parameters.description: The complete list of email addresses that should be invited, replacing everyone currently on the event. Anyone already invited keeps the kind of invitation they hold, so an optional guest stays optional. Leaving a booked room off the list is refused, since that would release its booking. Pass an empty list to uninvite everyone. Cannot be combined with attendee_emails_to_add or attendees_to_remove. Defaults to leaving the invitation list unchanged.

parameters.name: expected_change_key
parameters.description: The change_key of the event version being edited, from a read taken immediately beforehand. When given, the edit is refused if the event moved on since that read, and nothing is written. Defaults to writing the edit without a version check, over whatever is there.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The form the body argument is written in. Set html only when the body you are passing actually carries HTML tags, as the body_html of an event that was read does -- declaring html over plain words stores them marked as markup and they render wrong. plain_text stores the body as written, escaping anything that looks like markup. Ignored when body is left out. Defaults to plain_text.

parameters.name: recurrence
parameters.description: The parts of the repeat rule to replace; each field left out keeps its current value. Defaults to leaving the repeat rule unchanged.

output.description: The event as it stands after the edit, with what was written, whether the write ran under a version check, and how the event was found.

body.value: Please come prepared with your quarterly updates and blockers.

tools.name: WhoAmI
tools.description:
Get information about the current user and their Outlook Calendar environment.

mailbox_timezone is the time zone this mailbox's dates are expressed in. It may be a
Windows name such as "Eastern Standard Time" rather than an IANA identifier - that
names a zone observing daylight saving, not a fixed offset. mailbox_timezone_source
says where it came from: "mailbox" and "mailbox_utc" mean the mailbox itself names
the zone, whereas "default_not_configured" (the mailbox names none) and
"default_unreadable" (the setting could not be read) mean UTC is a fallback this
toolkit applied, not a zone the mailbox is set to. On either fallback, do not tell
the user their mailbox is configured for that zone.

output.description: Get comprehensive user profile and Outlook Calendar information.

summary:
## Microsoft Outlook Calendar Toolkit

Arcade's Microsoft Outlook Calendar toolkit gives LLMs structured access to a user's Outlook Calendar via Microsoft Graph, enabling agents to read, create, modify, and manage calendar events and scheduling on behalf of authenticated users.

## Capabilities

- **Event discovery & reading:** List events over a time range, search by property (subject, attendees, organizer, importance, online status), retrieve full event detail including rich-text body and online meeting links, list recurring series instances, and check attachment metadata.
- **Scheduling & availability:** Find meeting times across a group of attendees with ranked slot suggestions, check free/busy schedules for specific windows, and surface per-attendee availability details.
- **Event creation & editing:** Create one-off or recurring events on the default or a named calendar, with support for HTML body, recurrence rules, and organizer delegation; update any subset of event fields (including attendees and recurrence) without touching the rest.
- **RSVP & forwarding:** Accept, decline, or tentatively accept invitations with organizer notification; forward meetings to new attendees.
- **Cancellation & removal:** Cancel organizer-led meetings with invitee email notification (irreversible), or silently remove non-organized events from your own calendar.
- **Calendar & identity context:** List all accessible calendars (own, shared, delegated), and retrieve the current user's identity and mailbox timezone configuration.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 via the **Microsoft** provider. See the [Arcade Microsoft auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/microsoft) for setup details.
